spacr.crashreport.RelayRefused:
The relay did not answer a hosted diagnosis.

:param reason: ``"quota"`` when a free daily limit is used up,
    ``"network"`` when the relay could not be reached or the network is
    forbidden, and ``"error"`` for any other refusal.
:param detail: what the relay or the network said, for the log.
:param scope: for a quota refusal, whose limit it was: ``"install"``
    (this install's questions), ``"global"`` (spaCR's shared free
    capacity) or ``"ip"``.
:param resets_at: when the limit resets, as an aware UTC datetime;
    defaults to the next 00:00 UTC.

The values are kept on the exception as ``reason``, ``scope`` and
``resets_at``.
Keep the reason, scope and reset time, and the detail as the message.
spacr.crashreport.ai_summary_prompt:
The fixed prompt that asks the user's own AI to summarise a report.

The AI sees only the anonymised summary, never the traceback, log or
settings, and what it writes is scrubbed again before it is sent.

:param summary: a summary from :func:`public_summary`.
:returns: the prompt.
spacr.crashreport.anonymous_report_notic:
Whether the one-time notice about anonymised reports is still to show.

:returns: ``True`` until :func:`mark_anonymous_report_notice_shown`.
spacr.crashreport.anonymous_reports_enab:
Whether any failure is sent as an anonymised report.

:returns: ``False`` for the choices that send nothing.
spacr.crashreport.classify_failure:
Return whether a failure is a fault or a user error.

A :class:`spacr.errors.ConfigurationError`, or any of its subclasses, is
a user error: a setting, a validation or a missing input the user can
fix. Anything else is a fault.

:param exception: the exception, when at hand.
:param traceback_text: a formatted traceback otherwise.
:returns: :data:`KIND_USER_ERROR` or :data:`KIND_FAULT`.
spacr.crashreport.diagnose_remotely:
Ask the relay's hosted model about an error, with no account.

Sends the anonymised summary and the scrubbed question, cut to
:data:`MAX_QUESTION_CHARS`, to ``/diagnose``. The answer is generated
advice, not a checked fix. Blocks, so call it off the GUI thread.

:param summary: a summary from :func:`public_summary`.
:param question: what the user asks; may be empty.
:param timeout: seconds the model may take.
:returns: ``{"advice": text, "model": model name}``.
:raises RelayRefused: with ``reason`` ``"quota"`` when the free daily
    limit is used up, ``"network"`` when the relay cannot be reached or
    the network is forbidden, and ``"error"`` otherwise.
spacr.crashreport.error_report_mode:
Return the "AI Error report" choice, a key of :data:`ERROR_REPORT_MODES`.

A profile that only ever turned the older on/off switch off reads as
``"off"``.

:returns: the saved key, or :data:`DEFAULT_ERROR_REPORT_MODE`.
spacr.crashreport.example_public_summary:
Build a summary from a made-up error, to show what a report holds.

The error's message names a plate file under the home folder, an
e-mail address and a token, so the example shows each one removed.

:returns: a summary built exactly as a real one is.
spacr.crashreport.fetch_allowance:
Ask the relay how much of today's free allowance this install has left.

A GET of ``/allowance?install_id=...``; it uses up nothing. Blocks, so
call it off the GUI thread.

:param timeout: seconds the request may take.
:returns: ``{"ai": {"best_left", "light_left"}, "reports_left",
    "pool", "resets_at"}`` with ``pool`` one of ``best``, ``light`` or
    ``exhausted`` and ``resets_at`` an ISO-8601 UTC time; ``None`` when
    the network is forbidden or the relay gives no answer.
spacr.crashreport.flush_report_queue:
Try to send every waiting report, oldest first.

Stops at the first report that has to wait again (no network, a server
error or the relay's quota), so an offline computer makes one attempt,
not twenty. Does nothing while another send is running.

:param timeout: seconds each post may take.
:returns: ``{"sent": n, "dropped": n, "kept": n}``.
spacr.crashreport.install_id:
Return this profile's random install id, creating it on first use.

The id is a random UUID, not derived from the computer, the user or the
network. The relay uses it only to share its free allowance fairly.

:returns: the id as a string.
spacr.crashreport.mark_anonymous_report_: Record that the notice about anonymised reports has been shown.
spacr.crashreport.mode_code_context:
Whether a choice adds each spaCR frame's source line to a report.

:param mode: a key of :data:`ERROR_REPORT_MODES`; defaults to the saved
    one.
:returns: ``True`` only for ``"all_code"``.
spacr.crashreport.mode_explains:
Whether a choice has the AI explain every failure in the console.

:param mode: a key of :data:`ERROR_REPORT_MODES`; defaults to the saved
    one.
:returns: ``True`` for the four "Summarize" choices.
spacr.crashreport.mode_sends:
Whether a choice files a failure of ``kind`` as an issue.

:param kind: :data:`KIND_FAULT` or :data:`KIND_USER_ERROR`.
:param mode: a key of :data:`ERROR_REPORT_MODES`; defaults to the saved
    one.
:returns: whether it is sent.
spacr.crashreport.network_allowed:
Whether a report or a hosted diagnosis may use the network at all.

:returns: ``False`` when :data:`NO_NETWORK_ENV` has a nonempty value other than
    ``0``, ``false``, ``no`` or ``off`` (ignoring case and surrounding
    whitespace), or spaCR runs in safe mode; ``True`` otherwise.
spacr.crashreport.next_reset_utc:
Return the next 00:00 UTC, when the relay's daily allowances reset.

:param now: the moment to count from; defaults to now.
:returns: an aware UTC datetime.
spacr.crashreport.public_summary:
Build the anonymised summary of an error that may be published.

Only the keys in :data:`PUBLIC_SUMMARY_KEYS` are present. The message is
passed through :func:`scrub_public_text` and cut to
:data:`MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS`; the frames are at most :data:`MAX_FRAMES`
``{file, function, line}`` records with the file as a basename, or
``<user-code>`` for a file outside spaCR, Python and its libraries.
No log, setting, environment variable or path is read into it.

:param exception: the exception, with its traceback.
:param traceback_text: a formatted traceback, used when no exception
    object is at hand (a failed pipeline run reports one as text).
:param module: the spaCR module key the error happened in, such as
    ``mask`` or ``measure``.
:param user_note: what the user adds, scrubbed and cut to
    :data:`MAX_NOTE_CHARS`; left out when empty.
:param dry_run: ask the relay to validate without filing; left out when
    false.
:param kind: :data:`KIND_FAULT` or :data:`KIND_USER_ERROR`; worked out
    by :func:`classify_failure` when empty.
:param code_context: add each spaCR frame's source line as ``code``.
    Frames of any other file never carry code.
:param screen: the screen's title as the user sees it, such as
    ``Mask``; at most :data:`MAX_SCREEN_CHARS` characters.
:param error_text: the error as the console showed it, scrubbed with
    its line breaks kept and cut to :data:`MAX_ERROR_TEXT_CHARS`.
:param message: the message to send in place of the exception's own,
    such as every problem a refused run found; a user error keeps its
    line breaks and may be :data:`MAX_USER_ERROR_MESSAGE_CHARS` long.
:param settings: the run's settings; their names and public values
    (:func:`public_settings`) and the source folder's input facts
    (:func:`public_input_facts`) are added.
:param log_text: the console text before the failure; its last lines
    are added, scrubbed (:func:`public_log_tail`).
:param run: ``{"stage", "elapsed_s", "dry_run"}`` of the failed run.
:param diagnostics: add the environment block
    (:func:`public_environment`) and the exception chain.
:returns: the summary, ready for :func:`submit_public_summary`.
spacr.crashreport.queued_summaries:
Return the reports waiting to be sent, oldest first.

Expired and surplus reports are deleted first.

:returns: the summaries.
spacr.crashreport.relay_url:
Return the relay address reports are posted to, without a trailing slash.

:data:`REPORT_RELAY_ENV` overrides :data:`REPORT_RELAY_URL` when it holds
an ``https://`` address, or an ``http://`` one on this computer.

:returns: the base address.
spacr.crashreport.scrub_public_text:
Remove anything personal from a short text that will be published.

Absolute paths (POSIX, Windows and network shares) become ``<PATH>``,
file names with a data or code extension ``<FILE>``, e-mail addresses
``<EMAIL>``, web addresses ``<URL>``, IP addresses ``<IP>``, host names
``<HOST>``, this computer's login name ``<USER>``, and anything shaped
like a key, token or long hexadecimal or base64 string ``<TOKEN>``. The
redaction helpers of :mod:`spacr.qt.ai.issue_report` run first, and these
stricter rules after them.

:param text: the text; anything else is turned into text first.
:param limit: the longest result, in characters; a longer one is cut and
    ends in ``…``.
:param keep_docs_urls: keep the public spaCR addresses in
    :data:`PUBLIC_DOCS_URLS`, for an AI answer that links the
    documentation; every other address still becomes ``<URL>``.
:returns: the scrubbed text on one line.
spacr.crashreport.set_anonymous_reports_:
Turn reports on or off, as the first-run notice's switch does.

On restores the default choice when the current one sends nothing;
off is ``"off"``.

:param enabled: whether reports may be sent.
spacr.crashreport.set_error_report_mode:
Save the "AI Error report" choice.

A choice that sends nothing also deletes every report still waiting, so
nothing queued before the change is sent after it.

:param mode: a key of :data:`ERROR_REPORT_MODES`.
:raises ValueError: for any other value.
spacr.crashreport.submit_public_summary:
Send an anonymised summary to the relay, or queue it for later.

Blocks for up to ``timeout`` seconds, so call it off the GUI thread, or
use :func:`submit_public_summary_in_background`. With reports off, or
the network forbidden, nothing is sent and nothing is stored.

:param summary: a summary from :func:`public_summary`.
:param timeout: seconds the post may take.
:returns: ``{"status": ...}`` with :data:`REPORT_SENT` (and
    ``issue_number``, ``issue_url``, ``deduplicated``),
    :data:`REPORT_QUEUED` (kept to try again), :data:`REPORT_DROPPED`
    (rejected, not retried) or :data:`REPORT_DISABLED`.
spacr.crashreport.submit_public_summary_:
Queue a summary now and send it on a daemon thread.

The summary is on disk before this returns, so a process that ends at
once still sends it the next time spaCR starts.

:param summary: a summary from :func:`public_summary`.
:param on_done: called with the outcome :func:`submit_public_summary`
    describes, on the sending thread.
:returns: the thread, or ``None`` when reports are off and nothing was
    queued.
Send the queued summary and hand the outcome to ``on_done``.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.HostedProvider:
spaCR's hosted assistant: advice from spaCR's relay, no account needed.

It sends only what :func:`_hosted_request` keeps, the anonymised error summary and
the question, to the relay's ``/diagnose`` route through
:func:`spacr.crashreport.diagnose_remotely`. The answer is generated advice and is
labelled as such. It is the default while network access is allowed unless a
configured vendor CLI is explicitly preferred (:func:`default_provider`). It is
unavailable when the network is forbidden
(:func:`spacr.crashreport.network_allowed`).
spacr.qt.ai.providers.HostedProvider.che:
There is no sign-in to check.

:returns: ``None``.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.HostedProvider.is_: Whether the hosted provider may be used: the network is allowed.
Nothing to install: the hosted provider is always present.
Nothing to sign in to: the relay needs no account.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.HostedProvider.sou: Say where answers come from, in place of a CLI's location.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.HostedProvider.str:
Ask the relay and yield its advice, then a line saying what it is.

:param messages: conversation history as ``{role, content}`` dicts;
    only the anonymised summary and the newest question leave this
    computer.
:param system: ignored; the relay holds spaCR's own prompt.
:param model: ignored; the relay chooses its free model.
:returns: iterator yielding the answer.
:raises HostedProviderRefused: when the request is refused because of a quota, a
    forbidden or unavailable network, or another relay error.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.HostedProviderRefu:
The hosted request gave no advice because of a quota, network or other relay error.

A :class:`ProviderFailed`, so the console writes the message as it
stands after "[AI error]".

:param message: the sentence the user reads.
:param reason: ``"quota"``, ``"network"`` or ``"error"``, from
    :class:`spacr.crashreport.RelayRefused`, kept on the exception as
    ``reason``.
Keep the reason; the message is the whole text shown.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.apply_provider_cho:
Save a provider choice and try to apply it to open consoles.

The choice is saved even when its configuration checks fail. Open consoles are given
the chosen provider when those checks pass, otherwise the fallback from
:func:`default_provider`, which can be another vendor CLI or ``None`` when the
network is forbidden. Exceptions while updating consoles are ignored.

:param name: a name from :data:`PROVIDER_CHOICES`.
:returns: whether the chosen provider passed configuration checks, regardless of
    whether updating every console succeeded.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.default_provider:
Return the provider the AI switch uses.

:param preferred: the provider Preferences names, or ``""``.
:returns: the matching ``preferred`` provider from :func:`configured_providers`;
    otherwise the first provider in that list, or ``None`` if it is empty. The
    hosted provider leads while the network is allowed; otherwise vendor CLIs are
    considered in their registered order. This is a configuration choice, not a
    guarantee of authentication, remaining quota or request success.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.effective_provider:
Return the name of the provider Preferences shows as chosen.

:param preferred: the stored preference; ``""`` (never chosen) means
    spaCR AI (free).
:returns: a name from :data:`PROVIDER_CHOICES`.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.explain_failure:
Return a cached explanation or request one from the selected provider.

After a local cache miss, spaCR AI (free) asks the relay's ``/diagnose`` with the
anonymised summary and :data:`spacr.crashreport.EXPLAIN_QUESTION`; a vendor CLI
answers :func:`spacr.crashreport.ai_summary_prompt` here
(:func:`write_report_summary`). The returned text can be used for the console and
the report's ``ai_summary``. After a local miss, this function attempts one provider
request; a relay reply can itself be cached. Blocks, so call it off the GUI thread.

:param summary: a summary from :func:`spacr.crashreport.public_summary`.
:param provider: the active provider, or ``None``.
:param timeout: seconds a vendor CLI may take; defaults to
    :data:`spacr.crashreport.AI_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT_S`.
:returns: ``{"text": explanation or "", "tier": "best"|"light"|"", "refused": "" or
    "quota"|"network"|"error"|"none"}``. A local cache hit or a completed provider
    call also includes ``"cause"``. ``"saved"`` is ``"local"`` for a local hit,
    ``"relay"`` for reused non-empty relay advice, or ``""`` for a fresh hosted
    reply; other branches omit it.

With no provider, return ``"refused": "none"`` without consulting the local cache.
Otherwise a valid explanation from :func:`spacr.crashreport.saved_explanation` is
reused before any request, for every provider. Cache entries can expire or be
evicted, and failed saves are ignored, so the same error can require another
request.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.hosted_allowance_t:
One line saying how many free hosted-AI questions are left today.

:param allowance: what :func:`spacr.crashreport.fetch_allowance`
    returns, or ``None`` when it is not known.
:returns: the translated line, or ``""`` when nothing is known.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.hosted_cli_hint:
The hint for connecting a CLI that uses the user's own provider account.

:returns: the translated sentence.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.hosted_daily_allow:
The free allowance of spaCR AI, as Preferences states it.

:returns: the translated sentence.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.hosted_refusal_mes:
The sentence shown when the hosted provider gives no advice.

:param reason: ``"quota"``, ``"network"`` or anything else.
:param scope: for a quota refusal, ``"install"`` (this install's daily
    questions are used), ``"global"`` (spaCR's shared free capacity is)
    or ``"ip"``.
:param resets_at: when the limit resets; defaults to the next 00:00 UTC.
:returns: the translated sentence; a quota refusal also carries
    :func:`hosted_cli_hint`.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.local_reset_time:
The time the free allowances reset, in this computer's local time.

:param resets_at: an aware datetime or an ISO-8601 string; defaults to
    the next 00:00 UTC.
:returns: ``HH:MM``, followed by the weekday when it is not today.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.usage_bar:
What the usage bar under the AI chat box shows for a provider.

For spaCR AI (free) the bar is the user's share of today's shared free
capacity, ``neurons_left / share_neurons``, from the relay's dynamic
allowance. For a vendor CLI there is no reliable usage source
(:data:`CLI_USAGE_TEXT`), so the bar is hidden and only a line is shown.

:param provider_name: the selected provider's name, or ``None``.
:param allowance: what :func:`spacr.crashreport.fetch_allowance`
    returned, for spaCR AI.
:returns: ``(percent or None to hide the bar, translated text)``.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.with_ai_summary:
Prepare a report to request or include an AI summary.

For spaCR AI (free), set ``summarize: true`` so report submission can request a
relay-written summary; this function does not contact the relay itself. A vendor CLI
writes the summary here (:func:`write_report_summary`) and a non-empty result is
included as ``ai_summary``. With no provider, or when the CLI gives no text, the
copied report data is unchanged.

:param summary: a summary from :func:`spacr.crashreport.public_summary`.
:param provider: the active provider, or ``None``.
:returns: a new summary dict.
spacr.qt.ai.providers.write_report_summa:
Have the user's own AI summarise an anonymised report, or return ``""``.

The provider is given :func:`spacr.crashreport.ai_summary_prompt` as a single user
message, and a worker thread collects its reply. If the worker is still running
after ``timeout`` seconds, cancellation is requested and ``""`` is returned; a
provider exception or an empty reply also gives ``""``. Blocks, so call it off the
GUI thread.

:param summary: a summary from :func:`spacr.crashreport.public_summary`.
:param provider: a vendor CLI provider, or ``None``.
:param timeout: seconds to wait; defaults to
    :data:`spacr.crashreport.AI_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT_S`.
:returns: the summary text, scrubbed and cut to
    :data:`spacr.crashreport.MAX_AI_SUMMARY_CHARS`.
spacr.qt.install_consent.AnonymousReport:
Show exactly what an anonymised error report holds, with an example.

The example is built by :func:`spacr.crashreport.example_public_summary`
from a made-up error whose message names a file under the home folder,
an e-mail address and a token, so the dialog shows each one removed.

:param parent: parent widget.
Build the explanation, the example and a Close button.

:param parent: parent widget, or ``None``.

The one-time notice that anonymised error reports are on by default.

Not modal: it never stands between the user and the window. Closing it
saves the switch as it is then.

:param parent: parent widget.
Build the notice, its switch and its two buttons.

:param parent: parent widget, or ``None``.
spacr.qt.install_consent.maybe_show_anon:
Show the anonymised-report notice once per profile, without blocking.

Nothing is shown while the network is forbidden
(:func:`spacr.crashreport.network_allowed`), since no report could be
sent; the notice then waits for a start that allows it. Waiting reports
are also given another try, on a background thread.

:param parent: the window that parents the notice.
:returns: the notice, already showing, or ``None`` when it was not due.
spacr.qt.preferences.PreferencesDialog._: The provider whose switch is on.
Use the provider just chosen at once, and say what it needs.
Open the example of an anonymised report.
spacr.qt.screens.app_screen.AppScreen._s: Explain, summarise and post the failure. Off the GUI thread.
spacr.qt.widgets.console_panel.ConsolePa:
Refresh the usage bar under the chat box for the selected provider.

For spaCR AI (free) the relay is asked, off the GUI thread, how much
of today's share is left; the request runs on a plain thread that
touches no Qt object, and a single-shot timer tied to this panel
collects the answer on the GUI thread, so a panel closed meanwhile
never hears back. A vendor CLI has no usage source, so its line is
shown at once and the bar is hidden
(:func:`spacr.qt.ai.providers.usage_bar`). No provider hides the row.
